$comment: THE CAPABILITY MODEL (docs/SIR_V04_PLAN.md F.1) — the single source of truth for
what the toolchain can actually DO, read by three consumers that must never
duplicate it: rdv (what it can verify), sir-factory pack (what it may stamp),
and the toolkit prompts (what a decomposer may propose).
specVersion remains the COARSE gate: an rdv predating this file ignores it and
still halts on a version it doesn't know, which must stay true (plan A6). This
file REFINES that for consumers who understand it — a bundle is verifiable when
every feature it declares is implemented here, so a partially-built v0.4 is
ADDING A FEATURE HERE IS A CLAIM THAT THE VERIFIER IMPLEMENTS IT. Do not add one
to unblock generation; that inverts the whole point (the version must track what
rdv can check, not what the schema has published).
`implemented` and `generable` are DIFFERENT claims and gate different things.
`implemented`: rdv can check a unit that uses this. `generable`: a decomposer may
EMIT it, earned only by the Phase 5 gate — cold re-emitters converge on it from
the SIR alone, with no schema and no prompt fragment. A feature can be verifiable
and still not safely writable, and shipping that pair backwards produces contracts

vectors.summary: frozen + held-out input/output vectors graded by quorum
vectors.generationEvidence: shipped factory record — the blind-quorum pipeline has emitted units using this feature since before fragments existed (colors, bcryptjs, request and the @rederive/* catalog); its generability is what the factory's whole history tests

trace-seam.generationEvidence: shipped factory record — the blind-quorum pipeline has emitted units using this feature since before fragments existed (colors, bcryptjs, request and the @rederive/* catalog); its generability is what the factory's whole history tests

scheduler.detect: the SIR declares a time.timer / microtask control effect
scheduler.summary: timers + microtasks on virtual time, resolution order deterministic
scheduler.evidence: rederive/experiments/v04-phase1-scheduler — both race branches reachable + replayable (50x each); the real-clock control ran 20/20 one way, never executing the other branch
scheduler.generationEvidence: rederive/experiments/v04-phase5-generation — 3/3 cold re-emitters on the first round; two of the three were BYTE-IDENTICAL. All armed one timer per event up front and broke ties by arm order. Controls rejected: a sort arming no timers (right answer, no scheduling) and a reverse-tie unit that passed the distinct-delay case and failed only on ties

lifecycle.detect: the SIR declares a cancellable resource (timer/handle/subscription)
lifecycle.summary: resource lifecycle asserted separately; catches leaks invisible to value+trace
lifecycle.evidence: rederive/experiments/v04-phase2-lifecycle — adversarial 3-channel proof + @fixture/lifecycle (correct VERIFIED 2/2, leaky FAILED 0/2 on the lifecycle field alone)
lifecycle.generationEvidence: rederive/experiments/v04-phase5-generation — 3/3 cold re-emitters on the first round; every one cleared the timer on the gate-wins path. Controls rejected on the lifecycle channel while returning the CORRECT value: a leaky unit that never cleared, and a lazy unit that armed only after awaiting

par-interleaving.detect: the SIR declares PAR over dependent sub-traces, or a concurrency bound
par-interleaving.summary: verification over the space of interleavings, with the rung reported honestly
par-interleaving.evidence: rederive/experiments/v04-phase3-par + v04-phase0-pmap — @fixture/par correct VERIFIED 2/2, completion-order-keyed FAILED 0/2; coverage stamped (8 and 54 schedules, exhaustive)
par-interleaving.generationEvidence: rederive/experiments/v04-phase5-generation — 3/3 cold re-emitters built it from the SIR alone (no schema, no fragments), position-keyed across all 4/8/54 exhaustive schedules. Round 1 was 1/3, and the 2 misses were NOT about PAR: all three agreed on the concurrency shape and diverged on whether the gate or the unit computed the mapping. Hardening that one sentence fixed it.

ring.summary: token-coordinated concurrency reduces to a deterministic schedule; checked as a refinement (safety) AND for token loss/duplication (liveness)
ring.evidence: rederive/experiments/v04-phase4-ring — R_ring subset R_free checked; recognition (preserving) vs imposition (refinement) distinguished; a fake ring caught. @fixture/ring correct VERIFIED 2/2, broken FAILED 0/2 | LIVENESS (Phase 4b): token channel held->passed|released asserts mutual exclusion + return; generic halt detection; @fixture/ring-live sound VERIFIED 1/1, lost and duplicated both FAILED 0/1 on units whose OUTPUT IS CORRECT
ring.generationEvidence: rederive/experiments/v04-phase5-generation — 3/3 cold re-emitters on the first round, no hardening needed: correct take/pass/release path, one holder at any instant, released exactly once, reduced to a single schedule. RING survived the blind test unaided.

$rungs.$comment: Verification STRENGTH, weakest first. A bundle records the rung it earned; a feature gates which rungs are AVAILABLE, never whether a unit may ship (plan design move 2).
